📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

Recent findings suggest that I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the latest Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

Industry observers note that some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-fresh information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:.

Yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

You can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

In a recent development, it's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

While it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar indicates it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

In a recent development, I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite fresh features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

Sources indicate that any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

Sources indicate that if you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with new statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

When you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

Recent findings suggest that when GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the big things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

It has been revealed that of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

Recent findings suggest that for now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

Sources indicate that anything here sound particularly enticing to you? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it is mentioned that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

In Swarmbreaker - which debuts on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

It has been revealed that the results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!".

"SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the fresh maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the fresh maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 right now is.

In a recent development, another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

According to recent reports, more Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off latest gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

In a recent development, battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios remarked we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

According to recent reports, ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of significant maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

According to recent reports, for context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios states it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A massive part of what’s giving Grand Theft Auto 6 its incredible hypnotic power over a statistically-significant portion of the gaming public is its gigantic, intricately-designed world. There are so, so many details to uncover all over the place if you take a moment to stop and look for them, and I’m not just talking about Bigfoot hanging out in the swamps or the many varieties of bird flying around. There are lots of little details that subtly inform aspects of the characters’ personalities and interests, including, apparently, the particular brands of power tools they prefer.

In a recent development, early in the game, after receiving word that one of the game’s protagonists, Lucia, is coming back from prison, our other lead, Jason, can work to fix up their bungalow home in order to preemptively improve his relationship level with her. This means undertaking a few assorted tasks like repainting and fixing the walls, re-shingling the roof, fixing the stairs, and so-forth.

According to recent reports, A certain subset of players couldn’t help but notice that the tools Jason uses when fixing the walls and roof are colored a distinct shade of yellow. The brand printed on the tool may be different from real-life, but fans of hardware know the distinct iconography of DeWalt when they see it.

It has been revealed that for those with no interest in power tools, DeWalt is one of the most prominent brands in the scene, manufacturing all of the usual implements like power drills, nail guns, circular saws, and all that other good stuff, usually powered by rechargeable battery packs. As is so often the case with this sort of thing, fans of DeWalt have something of an unofficial rivalry with fans of other major hardware brands, especially Milwaukee, whose tools are usually colored red.

Recent findings suggest that during Jason’s various household repair chores, he uses a couple of power tools colored the same shade of yellow as DeWalt’s, both emblazoned with the logo “DEVICE.” Obviously, Rockstar can’t just use DeWalt’s actual logo in its game without its permission (though I have a feeling DeWalt would’ve loved it if given the opportunity), but the particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable. Looks like Jason is a DeWalt man, and fans on the DeWalt subreddit are holding this up as a victory over the likes of Milwaukee.

The particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable.

Recent findings suggest that the particular implements that Jason uses seem to be at least partially inspired by real-life DeWalt tools. The driver he uses when fixing the walls is nearly identical to DeWalt’s 20V MAX 1/4 inch impact driver. The nail gun he uses to fix the fencing and roof doesn’t seem to have as close of a parallel, but it most closely-resembles the DeWalt 20V MAX XR brad nailer. That’s not a roofing-specific nailer, though, so either I’m wrong or Jason just doesn’t differentiate between nailer types. I’d believe either scenario.

It has been revealed that while this may seem like a granular detail to hyperfixate on, as I mentioned, it’s just kind of fun to examine every aspect of this simulated world. In addition to what I noted before about a character’s hardware preferences, it’s also interesting to hold up these simulated knock-off brands next to the real world.

A major part of the long-established aesthetic of the GTA world is riffing on aspects of real life. It’s always been a very exaggerated setting, often exemplifying the absolute worst parts of modern society for both laughs and drama. The fictional state of Leonida is pretty much Florida if it was slightly worse, and the same goes for Vice City and Miami.

According to recent reports, GTA has also parodied more than its fair share of real-life brands and corporations over its various entries, usually with much sillier, ruder names. Sprite becomes “Sprunk,” IKEA becomes “KRAPEA,” and Twitter becomes “Bleeter,” which I am sincerely happy did not change its name to “Blex” or something equally stupid since GTA 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Britain's Marc 'Caedrel' Lamont and Dan Gaskin were among the winners at the 2026 Esports Awards in Miami, where Counter-Strike 2 was named game of the year and Team Vitality and BLAST also took industry honours. The results crown a strong Counter-Strike year eight days before the next CS2 Major begins in Singapore.

The 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

The ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

It has been revealed that his co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

According to recent reports, gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

Counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

Vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

"When I won this award in 2023, I never thanked my parents" 😅❤️.

Esports Colour Caster of the Year — @DanGaskin pic.twitter.com/oZBw5FItEJ.

— Esports Awards Presented by Thunderpick (@esportsawards) November 18, 2026.

The team’s form held into the autumn. Vitality swept MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 grand final on 11 October. That was their second title in a row after winning StarSeries Fall in September.

The PGL Major Singapore 2026 runs from 25 November to 13 December with 32 teams and a US$1,250,000 prize pool, The Kallang reported. The final stages will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December.

If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

Industry observers note that for all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

So long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

Now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the significant national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

The biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

It may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have plans for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

While getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

According to recent reports, another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. At the moment, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

And, well, while I'm on the subject of plans, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the major money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

While Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

Sources indicate that I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

Industry observers note that I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a massive yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

According to recent reports, he completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

The next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

Except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI is out today, so a fair few people are going to disappear into Leonida for the foreseeable future. If you’re not one of them, the latest expansion for Disney Dreamlight Valley is also here, and after Gameloft’s near 30-minute showcase back in October, you can now actually play The Keepsake Sea.

According to recent reports, you can swim beneath the waves in a new Merfolk form, which comes with a wide range of customisation and colour options, and Dory from Finding Nemo joins you down there as the first Adventure Companion. She’ll help you uncover hidden items and hand out rewards of her own as well. That is, if she remembers.

Sources indicate that the new story is spread across three mysterious island Biomes, each with its own environments and underwater areas to explore. Five new Villagers come along with it. Captain Jack Sparrow is the obvious name, but you’re also getting Captain Hook and Wendy from Peter Pan, Megara from Hercules and Milo Thatch from Atlantis: The Lost Empire.

Further into the story, you’ll unlock your own Enchanted Pirate Ship, which you can customise and sail around The Keepsake Sea with a crew of Villagers on board. There are upcoming Character Houses and Decoration Blueprints too, plus more decorative items, as always.

Industry observers note that on Apple Arcade, the expansion comes with your subscription at no extra cost, as the earlier ones did. Three paid expansions in, I think that makes Arcade the easiest way into the Valley by some distance. The catch is that there’s no Star Path or Premium Shop in the Arcade Edition, and your save won’t move outside Apple’s own devices, so anyone with a well-established Valley on Switch would be starting from scratch.

Meanwhile, the next free patch, ʻOhana Holidays, arrives on December 9th, bringing Lilo to Disney Dreamlight Valley for a reunion with Stitch alongside upcoming seasonal content and Friendship Quests.

For something else to explore in the meantime, check out our list of the best adventure games on iOS.

Original Story: With GTA 6 reviews now out in the wild, and countless Xbox players already getting access to it via the controversial Newly introduced Zealand trick, it's no surprise that we've also got loads of screenshots and clips doing the rounds online.

One of the best sources for raw Xbox gameplay footage is the YouTube channel Fuzion Xbox Testing, and they're already uploaded their initial look at both the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S versions of GTA 6.

According to recent reports, on Xbox Series X, it's very much what you'd expect - a really amazing-looking game with an internal resolution of 1440p, upscaled to 4K. The 30FPS performance is largely smooth, but does drop frames on occasion.

I also played GTA 6 on Xbox Series X for our Pure Xbox review, and here's what I remarked about it:.

Recent findings suggest that "Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well...".

"It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.".

In a recent development, on Xbox Series S, GTA 6 still looks really impressive from a visual standpoint, even though some drawbacks have clearly been made in terms of ray tracing and texture quality. The frame rate in the game's initial opening is shown to be a locked 30FPS in some sequences, dropping into the mid-20s during busier moments.

It has been revealed that overall though, the feedback we've seen from Xbox Series S players thus far has been very positive, especially in terms of how impressive the game looks. Rockstar Games actually talked to Wccftech about the Series S version as well, revealing they're using AMD FSR Upscaling 4 to scale the resolution to 1080p.

"On the Xbox Series S, we’re starting from a base resolution of 720p, which is scaled to 1080p using AMD FSR Upscaling 4.".

It has been revealed that "...[our] focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming.".

Great stuff, then! We'll leave you with the comparison footage for GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S down below.

According to recent reports, are you playing on either console yet? What do you think of the visuals and performance? Tell us in the comments.

#40659. Tech Report: Massive Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

Tech Report: Massive Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that friendslop du jour Massive Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!).
  • A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset.
  • Sources indicate that so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that friendslop du jour Massive Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.".

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who remarked it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

Sources indicate that so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Substantial Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest.".

In a recent development, if I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Major Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:.

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together.".

Until November 21st, the Fan Zone at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix has Hello Kitty Island Adventure set up to play at the F1A Paddock. There’s also a Hello Kitty Cafe Pit Stop doing baked treats, a Creative Garage for a bit of arts and crafts, and a Hello Kitty and Friends photo wall too.

Sources indicate that F1 Academy, for the uninitiated, is the all-female series that runs alongside Formula 1, and Sanrio first teamed up with it at last year’s finale in Vegas. I do like that the game gets something out of it, too, since most of us are nowhere near Nevada, and a grandstand and some merch don’t do a lot for you from the sofa.

In a recent development, the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

Industry observers note that his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

According to recent reports, the rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

Sources indicate that that deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

Industry observers note that the overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

Industry observers note that A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

It has been revealed that for the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert states Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The newly introduced hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games.
  • "Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of upcoming mods at the moment uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making.
  • Sources indicate that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the new "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of upcoming mods at the moment uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon.".

Sources indicate that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the new "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is important for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the issue for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected.".

Recent findings suggest that the All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the Newly introduced Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one newly introduced mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

In a recent development, personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for upcoming mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this patch does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since its release earlier this year, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has gotten plenty of praise for capturing the grit and horrors of the jungles of Vietnam. At the same time, the game has also been on the receiving end of criticism for its rather limited arsenal.

Industry observers note that the dev team over at Expression Games has taken that to heart. After addressing the two more glaring omissions by adding the American M14 and the Soviet SKS, the most iconic Western weapon of the Cold War is finally making its way to Southeast Asia.

The next big release for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, patch 2.0, is bringing the FN FAL into the fray, specifically in its British version that saw combat in the region.

Introduced in 1953, the FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

Recent findings suggest that chambered for the same 7.62x51mm NATO as the M14, M40 and M60 already in the game, the L1A1 SLR (Self-Loading Rifle) variant comes with a 20-round box magazine and is limited to semi-automatic fire. This was a design choice by Commonwealth clients, and really, unless you want to shoot down NVA planes while aiming at the horizon, you won’t notice the difference.

In a recent development, in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, the L1A1 will be available to the United States & Allies faction to represent its service with Australian and New Zealander units deployed there. Unlike the M14, the new rifle won’t be available to the Rifleman role.

The FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

To use the L1A1, you’ll need to reach level 6 in one of the following roles:.

I want to caveat here that if you actually pick the L1A1 over the M60 while playing machine gunner, you are a bad person and your team will be short in firepower. MG roles are for pouring it on downrange, not for reloading after twenty shots, and I’m saying this as a staunch FAL defender.

The developers have not offered any insight on how the pilots are supposed to fit a rifle that long in the cockpit of the Huey, but we can look the other way for a little bit.

As much as I’m pining for the L1A1 and it will be my personal highlight of revision 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, it’s hard to argue against the real significant item on the prospective patch notes being the Khe Sanh map and what it means for the game as a whole.

Khe Sanh will be the debut map for the Assault game mode, doubling down on the attackers versus defenders gameplay already present in the Offensive mode.

Assault brings back a fan favorite from the World War 2 Hell Let Loose, and focuses specifically on horrific trench warfare, strongpoints, and choosing whether you prefer dying in a fatal funnel in a trench or getting ripped apart by artillery out in the open. It’s great fun once you get used to the tinnitus.

Level designer Kienan Suthar provides more detail in this deep dive:.

The battle of Khe Sanh was one of the toughest battles in the Vietnam War, coinciding with the Tet Offensive of January 1968 and lasting until July of that same year.

In a recent development, khe Sanh Combat Base was surrounded by a large North Vietnamese force, supported by Viet Cong and Pathet Lao rebels. For five months, US and allied forces reinforced the base primarily from the air, while throwing everything and the kitchen sink at the Vietnamese troops.

In a recent development, the outcome of the battle, as many major engagements of the Vietnam War, was inconclusive. The North Vietnamese siege was partially lifted by April 1968, but a shift in US strategy in the aftermath of the Tet Offensive led to its abandonment on July 9.

For the Americans, avoiding a Điện Biên Phủ situation and preventing the collapse of the base was considered a win. The North Vietnamese, meanwhile, celebrated victory by capturing the region following the withdrawal.

For players, the real tangible outcome is that it created an incredibly dense network of fortifications for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam to sink its teeth into the assault mode.

Sources indicate that update 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is scheduled for the first half of December. Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is currently available on PC, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X/S.

According to recent reports, download now! PUBG Mobile Flash.

Sources indicate that A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Recent findings suggest that skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

In a recent development, skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

Industry observers note that after weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The proposal is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

According to recent reports, we’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one upcoming map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a fresh matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Recent findings suggest that things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a upcoming Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

Recent findings suggest that the Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s.
  • I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on rapidly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer.
  • Industry observers note that seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on rapidly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Industry observers note that seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his plan.

According to recent reports, as for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

In a recent development, fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as fresh minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with upcoming special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

In a recent development, beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds fresh palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.
