💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 revision is huge.
  • Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.
  • The team began planning the 3.0 revision two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Organization of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 revision is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with latest autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

The team began planning the 3.0 revision two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Organization of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio.".

Industry observers note that relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Company of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel indicates. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'.".

Sources indicate that complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added newly introduced units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie indicates. "It was a lot.".

In a recent development, as the 3.0 update grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Organization of Heroes 3, we were going to have an glitch that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a upcoming Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel says.

According to recent reports, further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the significant 3.0 upgrade release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Manufacturer of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie states." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 update that we had a major spike of users and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well.".

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

The next release for Company of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the upgrade, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding new units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

In a recent development, after that, though, I ask if Relic intends to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a latest project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing.".

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate….

According to recent reports, if I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Tech giant’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly quickly.

In a recent development, as it currently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming patch, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in Upcoming Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

Recent findings suggest that the narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for Latest Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

It has been revealed that the story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with newly introduced maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Industry observers note that angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sources indicate that sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

It has been revealed that aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

In a recent development, version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

It has been revealed that beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The substantial event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.

Recent findings suggest that though it may seem like we just had a massive life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

In a recent development, the game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab declared today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

In a recent development, the developer mentioned to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

Industry observers note that starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

Recent findings suggest that on top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab claims you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their intends for the shooter making some substantial promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

Industry observers note that the previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the fresh runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few upcoming weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

  • Fans of the Grand Theft Auto franchise were frustrated by the numerous delays and gaps in announcements for the sixth entry in the franchise.
  • On November 19, 2026, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launched, and many people were there on day one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 cost a lot of money to make, but Rockstar and Take-Two’s gamble paid off, bringing in three times its initial billion-dollar budget.

Fans of the Grand Theft Auto franchise were frustrated by the numerous delays and gaps in announcements for the sixth entry in the franchise. While many believed this was a positive sign, as it proved Rockstar wasn’t going to run the game out the door, it also led to speculation about a project that was facing troubles behind the scenes, like many titles before it.

On November 19, 2026, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launched, and many people were there on day one. The true scope of Grand Theft Auto 6’s success has been revealed by Take-Two in a statement to Variety, revealing just how much money the game has made so far.

According to Take-Two, Grand Theft Auto 6 has made over $3 billion, triple its production budget. The entire day-one take (including pre-orders) was 32.5 million units sold, making it the single biggest entertainment launch of all time and beating anything produced by big names like Minecraft, Star Wars, Marvel, or Harry Potter.

It is worth mentioning that this is only the console launch for two platforms, as Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently available only on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X/S. The PC release in 2027 is also expected to be huge, and if Rockstar can get the game running on the Switch 2, then Nintendo fans can join in too.

There’s also the future to consider, as Grand Theft Auto 6 is having some performance woes on the current hardware. If Rockstar has an enhanced version waiting for the PlayStation 6 and XBOX Project Helix, then that’s even more money coming in. That might take a while, however, as those platforms aren’t expected until 2028 at the earliest, and if hardware prices keep rising, no one will buy them.

The entire day one take (including pre-orders) was 32.5 million units sold, making it the single biggest entertainment launch of all time, beating anything produced by the major names, like Minecraft, Star Wars, Marvel, or Harry Potter.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is right now only a single-player game, which means the inevitable successor to Grand Theft Auto Online is still coming. Grand Theft Auto Online helped propel Grand Theft Auto 5 to the status of the second-best-selling video game of all time, and the same could well happen for its sequel.

Recent findings suggest that it’s safe to say that Rockstar and Take-Two’s multiple delays for Grand Theft Auto 6 paid off. The game could have been rushed out in an incomplete state back in 2025 or 2026, but as Cyberpunk 2077 proved, that can completely ruin a series’ reputation, and Rockstar would have had to work hard to earn it back.

As it stands, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most highly acclaimed and best-reviewed video game of all time, with relatively few performance problems and glitches at launch. If it had introduced in a rough state, that would have tanked the review scores, which will be a huge part of the game’s post-launch ad campaign.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the biggest media moment in recent memory, and it’s just getting started. With more platforms and the online mode still on the way, there’s no telling just how far the game will go. Perhaps the time has come for a video game to finally outsell Minecraft, a feat that no one thought possible, but may finally come to pass.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.

The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be stated for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.

According to recent reports, it also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.

If you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere. Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.

Ready? Let's dive right into things...

Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.

In a recent development, batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.

Steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones-style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.

Sources indicate that however, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.

A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party, followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.

Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.

It has been revealed that this one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

One of the few games Europeans got which never saw the light of day in North America, Disaster: Day of Crisis is a Monolith Soft joint that showcases the Wiimote's versatility with different control schemes across its four main gameplay styles, which naturally includes those video game staples, shooting and driving.

The latter is handled with the Remote held horizontally, while outside the Nunchuk-controlled walking sections, the game becomes a pointer-based rail shooter.

In a recent development, with a blockbusting story that crams in volcanoes alongside shady outfits and plenty of (melo)drama, it doesn't quite cohere as it should, and there are certainly better-looking titles on the system. But as a curio from a studio with an enviable pedigree — and a game that apparently didn't pass Reggie Fils-Aimé's quality bar for release — it's a fascinating glimpse at Monolith's Wii-era thinking before Xenoblade Chronicles dropped two years later.

Excite Truck was an underrated gem in the Wii's early life, with satisfying motion controls that paired beautifully with the wallow-y physics of the arcade monster trucks you raced.

In a recent development, it also let you load up MP3s on your SD card and make your own soundtrack, which felt like a bit of magic to some Wii gamers (read: this Wii gamer) back in 2006. Nothing like boosting over a canyon with Gwen Stefani booming through the speakers. Good times.

Having recently fired up Excite Truck, I can confirm that this holds up beautifully, with subtle controls and a suitable sense of heft and face-blasting speed. Helluva game.

It has been revealed that excitebots, Monster Games' 2009 follow-up, kept the arcade sensibilities and challenging terrain but switched out the trucks for on-wheel robots. It's a fantastic game that injects a little more personality into the basic structure of Excite Truck while keeping the speed and excitement.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, it's also a game which never rolled out in Europe, so we're right now tit-for-tat after Disaster: Day of Crisis. North America got the better deal, there.

Look, it's an inconsequential Zelda spin-off designed to showcase the Wii Zapper, but it is a system-exclusive inconsequential Zelda spin-off. Can you afford not to have it in your collection?

According to recent reports, hmm, probably. There's a reason this target-practice game is bottom of our Zelda list. Still, it's not unenjoyable, still dirt cheap, and it's got Twilight Princess-era Link on the box. I've somehow ended up with two copies. One of those 'oh, I don't have this' moments when you get home and realise 'yes, I already have this.'.

Another 'built for Wii' game that came to other platforms later (Vita in 2012, PC in 2016), Cing's Little King's Story added dashes of Doshin The Giant and Pikmin to a real-time strategy tale of the titular diminutive king working to expand the reach of his kingdom one citizen at a time and conquer neighbouring territories,.

An engaging genre mash-up that holds its own alongside the previously mentioned Pikmin series while putting a fresh spin on things, this was one of the last games Cing (Hotel Dusk, Another Code) released. Two years later, the company filed for bankruptcy.

When PlatinumGames' name is on the box, you expect style - and MadWorld certainly delivered that with its inky, Sin City-esque aesthetic that splattered blood red across a black-and-white canvas.

At a time when all the serious games elsewhere were shiny and brown and grey, this Sega-published chainsaw-'em-up also helped demonstrate that Wii wasn't only a console for fluffy technicolour worlds and cuddly mascots.

It has been revealed that as a hack-and-slash brawler, it's not up there with the developer's finest work - there's definitely an element of style over substance here. But when the style is this good, it's still worth the space on the shelf.

Honestly, at this point we all thought we'd have access to this on Switch one way or another — via NSO if not a proper remaster. However, at the time of writing (and discounting the now-unavailable Wii U eShop release of the Trilogy), this Metroid is still a Wii exclusive.

We can only assume it will arrive at some point — Nintendo now has the four Pikmin games on Switch, so it's about time to plug the Prime gap, too.

And staying on that theme, let's stick with Samus over the page...

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

In a recent development, at the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

According to recent reports, this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is right now number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

According to recent reports, there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Industry observers note that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here after years of waiting and has somehow managed to surpass the ridiculous expectations set up by its predecessors and advertising. While sales and reviews are both at an all-time high, making GTA 6 officially one of the best games ever released, one aspect fans are still struggling with is the game's performance on consoles.

While the PlayStation Pro fares a bit better than the competitors, one of the most common complaints about the monolithic GTA 6 experience comes from a few visual and accessibility choices that can thankfully be fixed with a few simple adjustments.

Although fans are still stuck with a 30fps cap until the PC version releases, players like kidxvintage on X have been urging others to rush to their settings menu and change a few simple things, which has been described as making for a "night-and-day experience.".

For the settings you'll want to adjust, the most common recommendations are turning off motion blur to reduce the smear when moving your camera, in addition to disabling camera shake and camera bob entirely for a smoother cinematic experience, as well as setting the steering dead zone to 7 on your analog sticks for more control when driving.

While the recommendations have received plenty of support, other players have responded with their own optimal settings like lowering the dead zones and turning up aiming sensitivity, while noting that leaving motion blur on helps cover up GTA 6's stuttering when the frame rate drops below 30 during action sequences.

While players can't seem to agree on the exact values for each setting, it's clear that if you want to make the most out of your GTA 6 experience, especially now that missions aren't replayable anymore, the settings you'll want to experiment with to see what you like best come from the following areas:.

The best part is these settings can apply to just about any console you play on, whether it's a powerful PlayStation 5 Pro or the Xbox Series S that has been surprising players with its performance running GTA 6 so far, helping make the massive title even more accessible to players around the world.

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain organization finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are right now technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business complications they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing promptly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

Recent findings suggest that zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

Industry observers note that this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony noted that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring newly introduced creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was revealed back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a upcoming name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on mobile, point-and-click adventures feel right at home. Instead of clicking with a mouse, you can tap objects, and it often feels very intuitive. As such, they're a favourite among our App Army readers. So, whenever one comes along, we like to get their thoughts. This week, we've given them the spooky Cult Vacui. Here's what they stated:.

I love the atmosphere you have 24 mins to complete a ritual before you. Get possessed by a demon. The atmosphere is very good, and the artwork is great. My only problem is I have fat fingers. So selection can be difficult. The idea is that certain actions can take up your time. A bit like Blue Prince, I think.

You repeat until you work out the sequence of events. To be honest, I’m not so good at point-and-clicks, but the story and atmosphere keep me hooked. Just the touch controls feel fiddly. The artwork is a nice pixel style. Very much like the classic Lucas art games.

I’m not usually good at point-and-clicks, so what really grabbed me here is the unique time-management mechanic. Every action ticks down the clock, creating tension without real-time panic. I definitely struggled at first and died a few times trying to get it right,.

Thankfully, the manual save system (allowing you multiple save points) helped me go back and try different strategies. Combined with the eerie graphics and creepy atmosphere, it was much more enjoyment than frustration. It's a short (about two hours) atmospheric winner on iOS.

Cult Vacui is an old-school point-and-click adventure where you play as a man possessed by a demon and must find a way to exorcise the demon. In the first part of the game, you have a limited number of moves to get rid of the demon. This involves finding and manipulating objects to perform an exorcism ritual.

The graphics are atmospheric and pixelated and look like a PC game from the 90s. There is no hint function, and the tight number of moves can make the first part of the game frustrating. Saying that I enjoyed playing this adventure. I recommend it.

According to recent reports, cult Vacui is a pixel art stylised point-and-click survival horror game. Right from the start, I was pulled into CV’s handcrafted 19th-century setting. Puzzles can be difficult with no hand-holding, and every action takes time away from your 25-minute countdown, adding a real sort of tension to your playthrough.

The whole retro vibe works great too; the minimalistic colour tones of the graphics, along with its eerie soundtrack, create just the right amount of spookiness. Cult Vacui fits perfectly on mobile and deserves a spot on your device. What is the App Army? The App Army is Pocket Gamer's lovely community of mobile game experts. Sources indicate that right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

Recent findings suggest that I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

When it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

It has been revealed that there are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, upcoming reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

According to recent reports, the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Industry observers note that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

In a recent development, however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Fresh Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Industry observers note that furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Recent findings suggest that kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

According to recent reports, this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

It has been revealed that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no confirmed platforms.

In a recent development, although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

10 Best Easter Eggs in GTA 6

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1442 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the most common thing for any game developer to do is to make nods to different franchises in their game.
  • Whether you are a fan of games, television shows, or movies, there’s plenty to discover in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Maybe you have gone searching for the literal easter egg.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the most common thing for any game developer to do is to make nods to different franchises in their game. Affectionately called easter eggs, these little details are meant to be surprises for players who love various other franchises.

Whether you are a fan of games, television shows, or movies, there’s plenty to discover in Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar has taken the time to hide trophies all around Leonida for those who are diligent enough to go searching for them. Even 'Weird Al' Yankovic is hiding in this game somewhere.

Have you found Dexter’s apartment? Maybe you have gone searching for the literal easter egg. Either way, these are amazing nods to other franchises in the mighty GTA 6.

Dexter is a very popular television series about a vigilante serial killer. This serial killer just so happens to live in Miami, which just so happens to be the city that Vice City is based on. What a coincidence!

It just so happens that Rockstar noticed this connection and decided to add a few nods to the series in GTA 6, with the first of them being Dexter’s apartment, which is located on Washington Island.

In a recent development, of course, you won’t be able to reach this area right away, but once you get access to the map, you can head straight there to check it out and pay tribute to the television series. You can also find some tools on the roof.

Industry observers note that bigfoot has decided to make his way out of the northern forests and headed south to the marshlands of Leonida. It’s a bit weird that he decided to make this island paradise his home, but I won’t question that.

If you progress through the story of GTA 6, there is a mission that will set you on the path to discovering Bigfoot, but he is easy to overlook, as he runs away rather quickly once you get near him.

Industry observers note that I barely caught a glimpse of him, but chased him down and caught a photo before he mysteriously disappeared into the marsh. I have no idea if I will see him again, but it was cool to catch a glimpse of this mysterious figure.

Sources indicate that some developers make nods to different games or pop culture, but Rockstar takes the time to put a literal easter egg in its game. That’s right, if you go to the correct spot on the map, you can find a nest with literal easter eggs in it.

Sources indicate that the location in question is a radio tower in South Vice Dale County. The radio tower takes multiple minutes to climb, but the payoff is definitely worth it, as you find a nest full of easter eggs at the top.

While I won’t spoil what happens when you throw one, it does involve a cutscene, and you should definitely take the time to visit the location and watch it unfold.

Sources indicate that one of the most memorable missions in GTA 5 is when Michael’s boat gets stolen and you need to chase down the people responsible. Unfortunately, Michael’s boat doesn’t get returned, but we now know the whereabouts of it, and it turns out that it landed in Jason’s yard.

It has been revealed that next to Jason’s house, there is a run-down boat that looks similar to Michael’s. People have pointed this out for a while, but there was no confirmation until now.

According to recent reports, since the game is officially out, you can check out the boat, and you can even climb on top of it. Once there, you can use your phone’s camera to check out the display. Doing so will allow you to see a display that shows part of the GTA 5 map, seemingly confirming that this is Michael’s boat.

It has been revealed that have you ever heard of a movie called Island Claws? If not, you aren’t the only one, but there is a nod to this film in GTA 6. The movie is from the 1980s, and it is about a scientist who genetically modifies crabs to make them grow larger to solve world hunger.

Unfortunately, this doesn’t work out very well, and a similar thing has transpired in Leonida. In Pelican Valley, you can find a trail of blood that leads to a shack. Inside the shack, you can find information about failed experiments on crabs.

Along with this, Jason will get attacked by a giant crab that jumps down on him from the ceiling. It is a rather large easter egg that is meant to pay homage to the classic independent film. Good job doing your research Rockstar.

One of the things that people loved to do in Grand Theft Auto 5 was break into the military base, and the go-to means of breaking into the base was via the hill jump just outside the fence along the highway.

Well, there is another military base in GTA 6 and it is located near where you start the game. It is called Mile Zero Air Station, and it has a convenient hill just outside the fence that you can use to jump into the base just like in GTA 5.

According to recent reports, there is no way that this is a coincidence because the hill is an obvious jumping point. Thank you Rockstar for including an obvious homage to the previous game and the silly antics players got into.

Industry observers note that the most common meme that has ever been spread about a video game is probably the, “We got [insert item here] before GTA 6.” It popped up every single time something major happened before the release of the game. Well it can’t be mentioned anymore since the game is out.

With that being mentioned, the meme will probably become about either Elder Scrolls 6 or GTA 7, or maybe even RAC 7. You might be wondering what that is. Well, if you scroll through your phone’s Snapmatic app, you can find a post about a game called Barnyard Blue: Hot Pursuit.

The post reads, “Barnyard Blue video game before Race and Chase 7 is crazy.” There is even a comment that reads, “We really got Barnyard Blue games before RAC 7.” This is, of course, a jab at the classic meme that appeared for so many years.

It has been revealed that the X-Men actually exist in the Grand Theft Auto universe, except they don’t exist in the same way as you know them. Instead of being called the X-Men, they are referred to as the RX-Men. A strange choice, but one that makes it obvious that it is a reference to the classic hero team.

There are various magazines that you can find in the different convenience stores around Leonida, but you can reliably find this magazine in the 24-7 supermarket in northern Key Lento.

In this story, you can find a copy of RX-Men glitch 13 titled, “Paging Dr. Placebo.” It features GTA renditions of different heroes and villains. There’s also collectible cards for these characters sprinkled around Leonida.

Speaking of trading cards, you can find various wrestling trading cards across Leonida. This is an obvious easter egg to the various wrestling trading cards that already exist. The wrestling tech giant is called B.A.M, and it stands for Backyard American Mania.

According to recent reports, florida has a rather large wrestling scene, with the WWE training facility being in Orlando. On top of this, various famous wrestlers live or lived in Florida.

To go even further, the acronym of B.A.M. can also be related to Bird Azarian Memorial Training Center, which is located in Illinois, but is a wrestling training center. Odds are, it is just a reference to WWE wrestling.

According to recent reports, early in the game, Jason and Cal sit down to play some games on the JoyStation, with the system itself being an obvious reference to the PlayStation 5. However, that isn’t the whole easter egg, as the game that is played is called Tenebrae Lux.

Tenebrae Lux is a game themed after the movie called The Lighthouse, which features both Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe. This is awesome, but there is yet one more easter egg hidden here.

The name Tenebrae Lux is Latin for the term “light-dark.” This happens to be the exact translation of the French term Clair Obscur, which is one of the greatest games to have been released in recent years and a game that took the world by storm.

#40604. Keeping hold of Organization of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO claims – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1078 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Keeping hold of Organization of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO claims – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • Sources indicate that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • According to recent reports, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Manufacturer of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Sources indicate that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Tech giant of Heroes provides.

According to recent reports, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell claims. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

Recent findings suggest that just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Recent findings suggest that anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell claims. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

In a recent development, relic and newly introduced owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Firm of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell claims foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly.".

Sources indicate that I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a significant part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Firm of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Firm of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a fresh game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

Recent findings suggest that as to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting the fan-favorite Firefight mode via a free update this winter, an Xbox Wire post confirms. The update will allow players to team up in cooperative wave-based PvE.

Industry observers note that firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry.

According to recent reports, xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan gets stronger by eating his own cooking.

Recent findings suggest that in an RPG, you’d expect to become stronger by hitting things, but in Kemco’s latest, you do it by eating your own cooking (abs are made in the kitchen, as the saying goes). Leingham Tavern Story: Alan and the Time Goddess is out now on the App Store and Google Play. It’s a dungeon crawler and a restaurant sim at the same time, and there’s an orphanage to save on top.

That orphanage is the whole reason you’re doing any of this. It’s about to close down, and Alan and his mates reckon a busy tavern will make enough money to keep it going. Which means heading down into dungeons for ingredients.

It has been revealed that you can go back to these every day, picking things up from gathering points and getting into turn-based fights with whatever monsters are lurking about. You’ll want better gear for the fights and you’ll want levels too, but like I mentioned, you get most of those from eating when you’re back.

Back at the tavern, you can buy recipes, and you can also mix ingredients yourself and see what you get. There are more than 800 dishes to find. There’s a field out the back for growing vegetables too, plus a fishing spot for when you fancy a break (apparently you can catch something you weren’t expecting, though I’ve no idea what).

It has been revealed that then there’s running the place, which is what actually keeps the orphanage going. Once a few dishes are on the menu, you open the doors, and from there it’s a case of changing what you cook to suit the season and whatever customers are into at the time, and working out which of your staff should be doing what. Leingham Tavern Story only comes in English and Japanese, and there’s no controller support either.

Leingham Tavern Story: Alan and the Time Goddess is out now on the App Store and Google Play for $9.99.

Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1377 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.
  • Industry observers note that you haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics.
  • I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

Industry observers note that you haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

It has been revealed that currently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

In a recent development, my computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

It has been revealed that I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is rolled out over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

It has been revealed that I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

Industry observers note that I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

The worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

Industry observers note that the main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Industry observers note that still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

According to recent reports, casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

How To Find The Kingfishers 22 Legendary Rifle Early In GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and you'll want to really maximize your firepower if you want to survive this dangerous world.
  • Sources indicate that however, you'll need to do a bit of fighting if you want to snag this weapon.
  • It has been revealed that to find the Kingfishers, you need to head to the Pelican Valley region in the southern portion of the map.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and you'll want to really maximize your firepower if you want to survive this dangerous world. To improve your chances of not becoming past tense, you'll want to find the various legendary-tier weapons hidden throughout Leonida. One of the earliest you can get is the Kingfishers W-22 small game rifle.

Sources indicate that however, you'll need to do a bit of fighting if you want to snag this weapon. If you're looking for an above-average weapon with solid accuracy, here is where to find the Kingfishers W-22 and what you need to do to acquire it.

It has been revealed that to find the Kingfishers, you need to head to the Pelican Valley region in the southern portion of the map. Specifically, we are looking for Wetman Bay, which is the southwestern portion of this region and is represented on your map by a bunch of tan islands. You can only reach this area by water, so make sure to use Jason's fishing boat to go to this area.

We are going to the Fishing Shacks, which are under the control of the Kingfisher gang. This area will become available after a few story missions, as Donnie will give you a side quest to go rob them and steal their cocaine. This will be marked on your map by a gold icon with a black crocodile on your map.

Recent findings suggest that I strongly recommend bringing a long rifle and to make sure you buff your health beforehand. There are quite a few enemies you'll need to fight through, so ensuring you have a way to promptly dispatch them is key. The shotgun is especially good here since the enemies have a bad habit of just rushing you, making it easy to kill them with this gun.

According to recent reports, when you arrive, deal with the Kingfishers and fight your way to the large red house that's sitting on a section of the dock over the water. Enter the house, kill the guard inside, and approach the table on the left side of the room. You'll see an open weapons case with the Kingfishers W-22. Additionally, you can find several bricks of cocaine around the room, all of which can be looted and sold back to Donnie or Brian in Key Lento.

There's also another small shed with a couple bricks of cocaine in the shed directly across from the crocodile the Kingfishers were skinning.

Sources indicate that as for the Kingfishers W-22, it will come with a red dot sight and a suppressor already attached. This makes it a great weapon if you're trying to accurately eliminate enemies from a distance, without causing a huge panic. It's also a solid hunting weapon if that does interest you; however, you'll want something with a bit more stopping power if you're killing big game.

Industry observers note that remember, even if you lose the Kingfishers W-22 it will be accessible in any weapons locker, making it nice to grab early and use whenever you want. Just make sure to store it in the trunk of your car so you don't cause a panic by running around with it!

As The Elder Scrolls 5 turns 15, massive mod Beyond Skyrim: Bruma gets a 2.0 update delivering a newly introduced quest, extra dungeons and an "expanded worldspace"
